items.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: once in 1911, that was right after the comet, Halley's Comet, we were in Atlanta.

ctx.x: And we could always stay as long as we'd want. Usually we'd always get three or four weeks by being able to change our act. And those Northern acts, we called them Northern acts because they all turned their noses up at us at first, you know, when they saw it. But what a riot we were when we finished our act. Then they come in to try to be friends. And so they used to come around and pat you on the back there and tell you, I'll find you, oh, I really enjoyed your act.
